# DevHub by Root Native (@rootnative/devhub)

> A CLI and a core library for Expo developers. DevHub keeps every Expo
> development build (dev client) on the machine, and installs a stored build
> on a running Android emulator or device, or on a booted iOS simulator.

Version: 0.0.0. This file describes this version only.

Source: https://github.com/rootnative/devhub

## What ships

- `devhub sync` downloads the EAS dev client builds of a project into the
  store, before EAS deletes them. `devhub sync --all` does this for each
  project that `devhub sync` saw before.
- `devhub list` shows the stored builds. `devhub where` gives the path of a
  build file.
- `devhub devices` lists the Android emulators and devices, and on macOS the
  booted iOS simulators.
- `devhub install` installs a stored build on a device that runs now.
- `devhub ui` serves a local page with the same functions, on 127.0.0.1.

NOT IMPLEMENTED, do not call: the fingerprint match, the Expo build cache
provider (`@rootnative/devhub/cache-provider`), the import of a build file,
the launch (boot a device, open the app), launch profiles, prune, and the
desktop app. They are the plan only.

## Requirements

- Node 20.19 or later. Run `npx @rootnative/devhub <command>`, or install
  the package globally to get the `devhub` command.
- For `devhub sync`: eas-cli with a login (`eas login` or
  `npx eas-cli login`). DevHub runs `eas` from `PATH`, or `npx --yes eas-cli`
  when `eas` is not on `PATH`. DevHub never reads, asks for, or stores a
  token.
- For Android: adb from the Android SDK Platform-Tools. DevHub uses the
  first `platform-tools/adb` in `ANDROID_HOME`, `ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`, or the
  default SDK folder of the system, and else `adb` from `PATH`.
- For iOS: Xcode, on macOS only.

## Rules for an agent

- Add `--json` to each command. Then stdout holds one JSON value and nothing
  else. Progress and warnings go to stderr.
- The exit code is `0` for success, `1` for a failure, and `2` for a usage
  error. After a failure, stdout is empty and stderr holds the message, with
  two exceptions. `devhub devices --json` prints its JSON and exits with `1`
  when each device tool fails. `devhub sync --json` prints its JSON and
  exits with `1` when a project fails.
- `<id>` is the EAS build ID, or a unique start of it. `devhub list --json`
  gives each full ID.
- `devhub install` does not start a device, and does not open the app.
  Start the emulator or the simulator first. Then run `npx expo start` in
  the project folder, and press `a` or `i`, to load the JavaScript.
- When two or more devices of the build's platform are ready,
  `devhub install` stops with exit code `2`. Give `--device <id>` with an ID
  from `devhub devices --json`.
- DevHub never uninstalls an app. For a signing key conflict, it prints the
  `adb uninstall` command and stops. An uninstall deletes the app data, so
  ask the user before you run that command.
- `devhub install` refuses an Android App Bundle (`.aab`), an iOS device
  build (`.ipa`), and each iOS build on Windows or Linux. `installProblem`
  in `devhub list --json` gives the reason and the fix before you try.
- `devhub ui` runs until Ctrl+C. To read data, use the commands with
  `--json`, not the page.
- Only one sync runs at a time. A second sync stops with exit code `1` and
  a message that names the process of the first one.
- A dev client is a debug build. Its JavaScript runs in development mode, so
  it does not show the speed of the app in production.

## CLI

### devhub

```text
DevHub by Root Native 0.0.0
Keep every dev build. Launch any one in one click.

Usage: devhub <command> [options]

Commands:
  sync          Download the EAS dev client builds of this project.
  list          Show the stored builds.
  where <id>    Print the path of a stored build file.
  devices       List the Android devices and the iOS simulators.
  install <id>  Install a stored build on the ready device.
  ui            Open the DevHub page in the browser.

Options:
  -h, --help     Show this help.
  -v, --version  Show the version.

Run "devhub <command> --help" to see the options of a command.
```

### devhub sync

```text
Usage: devhub sync [options]

Download each finished EAS dev client build of this project that the store
does not have. A build profile is a dev client profile when it has
"developmentClient": true in eas.json. DevHub runs "eas", or "npx eas-cli"
when eas is not on PATH, and uses the eas-cli login.

Options:
  --all             Sync each project folder that devhub sync saw before.
  --profile <name>  Also sync this build profile. Give it again for each
                    other profile.
  --dry-run         Show what the sync downloads. Download nothing.
  --json            Print the result as JSON.
  -h, --help        Show this help.

The store is in the data folder of the OS. Set DEVHUB_HOME to use a
different folder.
```

### devhub list

```text
Usage: devhub list [options]

Show the builds in the store, sorted by project and then newest first.
EAS EXPIRY is the date on which EAS deletes its copy. The copy in the store
stays.

Options:
  --json      Print the builds as JSON.
  -h, --help  Show this help.
```

### devhub where

```text
Usage: devhub where <id> [options]

Print the path of a stored build file. <id> is the EAS build ID, or the
start of it. "devhub list" shows a start of each ID that is unique.

Options:
  --json      Print the ID and the path as JSON.
  -h, --help  Show this help.
```

### devhub devices

```text
Usage: devhub devices [options]

List the Android emulators and devices that adb sees, and on macOS the iOS
simulators that run now. DevHub can install a build on a device in the state
"ready".

Options:
  --json      Print the devices as JSON.
  -h, --help  Show this help.
```

### devhub install

```text
Usage: devhub install <id> [options]

Install a stored build on a device that is ready: an Android build on an
emulator or a device, or an iOS simulator build on a booted simulator (macOS
only). <id> is the EAS build ID, or the start of it. "devhub list" shows the
builds, and "devhub devices" shows the devices. DevHub does not start a
device, and does not open the app.

Options:
  --device <id>  The adb serial or the simulator UDID of the device.
                 Necessary when two or more devices are ready.
  --json         Print the build and the device as JSON.
  -h, --help     Show this help.
```

### devhub ui

```text
Usage: devhub ui [options]

Start a local server for the DevHub page, and open the page in the browser.
The server listens on 127.0.0.1 only, and each run has a new token in the
URL. Press Ctrl+C to stop the server.

Options:
  --port <n>  The port of the server. The default is a free port.
  --no-open   Print the URL, and do not open the browser.
  --json      Print the URL and the port as JSON.
  -h, --help  Show this help.
```

## JSON output

- `devhub sync --json` prints `SyncReport`.
- `devhub list --json` prints `BuildList`.
- `devhub devices --json` prints `DeviceReport`.
- `devhub install <id> --json` prints `InstalledBuild`.

```ts
type SyncReport = {
    dryRun: boolean;
    projects: ProjectSyncResult[];
};

type ProjectSyncResult = {
    project: string;
    /** `missing`: the project folder does not exist. DevHub skipped it. */
    status: 'ok' | 'failed' | 'missing';
    profiles: SyncProfile[];
    builds: BuildOutcome[];
    warnings: string[];
    error?: string;
};

/** A build profile to sync, and the platforms whose builds DevHub keeps. */
type SyncProfile = {
    name: string;
    platforms: EasPlatform[];
};

type BuildOutcome = {
    id: string;
    status: BuildStatus;
    profile: string;
    platform: string;
    isForIosSimulator?: boolean;
    appVersion?: string;
    expirationDate?: string;
    /** Set when the status is `downloaded`. */
    path?: string;
    size?: number;
    /** Set when the status is `failed`. */
    error?: string;
};

type EasPlatform = 'ANDROID' | 'IOS';

type BuildStatus = 'downloaded' | 'would-download' | 'stored' | 'expired' | 'no-artifact' | 'invalid-id' | 'failed';

/** The JSON of `devhub list --json`. */
type BuildList = {
    /** Sorted by project, and then newest first. */
    builds: ListedBuild[];
    /** Build folders with no build.json. The next sync replaces them. */
    incomplete: string[];
    unreadable: UnreadableBuild[];
};

/** A build in the JSON of `devhub list --json`. */
type ListedBuild = {
    id: string;
    /** The absolute path of the build file. */
    path: string;
    size: number;
    sha256: string;
    storedAt: string;
    eas: EasBuild;
    /**
     * Why `devhub install` refuses the build on this system, with the fix.
     * Absent when it can install the build.
     */
    installProblem?: string;
};

type UnreadableBuild = {
    id: string;
    reason: string;
};

/**
 * One build as `eas build:list --json` prints it. eas-cli drops each field
 * with a `null` value, so an absent field means "no value". DevHub stores
 * the record without changes, so the type keeps the fields it does not know.
 */
type EasBuild = {
    id: string;
    platform: string;
    buildProfile?: string;
    distribution?: string;
    isForIosSimulator?: boolean;
    appIdentifier?: string;
    appVersion?: string;
    appBuildVersion?: string;
    sdkVersion?: string;
    runtime?: {
        version?: string;
    };
    fingerprint?: {
        hash?: string;
    };
    gitCommitHash?: string;
    gitCommitMessage?: string;
    app?: {
        id?: string;
        slug?: string;
        name?: string;
    };
    createdAt?: string;
    completedAt?: string;
    expirationDate?: string;
    artifacts?: {
        applicationArchiveUrl?: string;
        buildUrl?: string;
    };
    [field: string]: unknown;
};

/** The JSON of `devhub devices --json`. */
type DeviceReport = {
    devices: Device[];
    /** The error of each device tool that failed, with the fix. */
    warnings: string[];
};

type Device = {
    platform: DevicePlatform;
    kind: DeviceKind;
    /** The adb serial, or the simulator UDID. */
    id: string;
    name: string;
    /** The state as the device tool prints it. */
    state: string;
    /** DevHub can install a build on the device now. */
    ready: boolean;
    /** Why DevHub cannot install on the device now, and the fix. */
    problem?: string;
    /** The iOS version of a simulator. */
    osVersion?: string;
};

type DevicePlatform = 'android' | 'ios';

/** `physical`: a phone or a tablet that adb sees over USB or Wi-Fi. */
type DeviceKind = 'emulator' | 'physical' | 'simulator';

/** The JSON of `devhub install --json`. */
type InstalledBuild = {
    id: string;
    /** The absolute path of the build file. */
    path: string;
    device: Device;
};
```

- `devhub where <id> --json` prints `{ "id": string, "path": string }`.
- `devhub ui --json` prints `{ "url": string, "port": number }`, and the
  server then runs until Ctrl+C.

Each path is absolute. Each date is an ISO 8601 string. `eas` is the record
of `eas build:list --json` without changes, so it can have more fields than
the type names. eas-cli drops each field with a `null` value, so an absent
field means "no value".

## The store

One folder holds the builds of all projects. It is never inside a project
folder. Read it with the CLI. Do not write into it.

```text
<DEVHUB_HOME>/
  projects.json            each project folder that devhub sync saw
  sync.lock                the process ID of the sync that runs now
  builds/<easBuildId>/
    build.json             the record. A folder without it is incomplete.
    <file>                 .apk, .aab, .tar.gz (iOS simulator), or .ipa
  extracted/<easBuildId>/  the unpacked iOS simulator build, a cache
```

`DEVHUB_HOME` sets the folder. The default is
`~/Library/Application Support/devhub` on macOS, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\devhub` on
Windows, and `$XDG_DATA_HOME/devhub` or `~/.local/share/devhub` on Linux.

## Core API

`import { listBuilds } from '@rootnative/devhub'`. The package is ESM only,
for Node. The types are in `dist/index.d.ts`. The API can change in each
version before `1.0.0`.

Functions, classes, and constants: ADB_MISSING, BUILD_LIST_PAGE_SIZE,
DeviceError, EAS_ON_PATH, EAS_WITH_NPX, EasCliError, EasJsonError,
StoreLockedError, TAR_MISSING, XCRUN_MISSING, adbAvdNameCommand, adbDevice,
adbDevicesCommand, adbInstallCommand, adbInstallFailure, adbUninstallCommand,
artifactUrl, checkEasLogin, devClientProfiles, deviceReport, downloadFile,
easBuildListCommand, easWhoamiCommand, findBuild, findDevice, findEasProject,
findStoredBuild, installBuild, installPlatform, installProblem,
installStoredBuild, iosRuntimeVersion, isEmulatorSerial, isExpired,
listAndroidDevices, listBuilds, listDevices, listFinishedBuilds,
listIosSimulators, parseAdbDevices, parseAvdName, parseEasJson,
parseSimctlDevices, planSync, readEasJson, readProjects, resolveAdb,
resolveHome, runCommand, scanStore, selectDevice, simctlInstallCommand,
simctlListCommand, syncBuilds, syncFailed, syncProjects, tarExtractCommand,
unpackIosBuild, version, withExtraProfiles.

Types: AdbEntry, AdbInstallTarget, AdbOptions, BuildList, BuildOutcome,
BuildRecord, BuildStatus, Command, CommandOptions, CommandResult, CommandRunner,
Device, DeviceChoice, DeviceKind, DeviceList, DeviceListOptions, DevicePlatform,
DeviceReport, DeviceSource, DownloadResult, Downloader, EasBuild, EasInvocation,
EasPlatform, FindResult, FlowError, FlowResult, HomeOptions, InstallDeps,
InstallOptions, InstallRequest, InstalledBuild, ListedBuild, PlanItem,
ProfileBuilds, ProjectSyncResult, StoreScan, StoredBuild, SyncBuildsDeps,
SyncDeps, SyncOptions, SyncProfile, SyncReport, SyncRequest, UnpackOptions.
